result.title: Verifiable Efficiency Limits of Innate LLM Planning in Sliding Puzzles
result.summary: Tool-assisted planning success can reflect external search and verification, leaving a model's unaided planning ability unresolved. We isolate innate planning through complete plans generated in one response without tools or execution feedback. We propose a verifiable framework that decomposes success-weighted plan efficiency as $\mathrm{SPE}=R\times Q\times E$: execution reliability, planning coordination among legal plans, and action economy among completed plans. Trajectory replay and certified optima verify these factors; the joint score includes unsuccessful attempts. We evaluate 8,400 full-plan outputs from seven model conditions on $4\times4$ sliding puzzles, controlling exact horizon and obstacle count in the primary cohort. Models that complete every trial still become less economical at longer horizons, while higher efficiency among completed plans can coexist with poor goal attainment. SPE separates the overall capability hierarchy, while its factors distinguish coordination failure from inefficient completion. The framework makes long-horizon limitations in unaided planning quantitatively verifiable.

AI.brief_summary: 该论文在无工具、无执行反馈条件下让 LLM 一次性输出 4×4 滑块拼图的完整解，提出可验证的 SPE 指标，将计划效率分解为执行可靠性、合法计划间的协调质量与完成计划的动作经济性，并用轨迹回放与认证最优解核验，发现长时域下效率系统性下降。
